```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", error = FALSE)
```

In a three-way gravity model, exporter-year and importer-year fixed
effects account for country-specific conditions in each year. Directed
pair fixed effects absorb time-invariant differences between trade
partners. The agreement coefficient uses changes within pairs after
accounting for both country-year effects.

## Simulate trade across pairs and years

Each directed pair is observed in all eight years. Some pairs adopt an
agreement during the sample. The first two pairs have no trade in any year.

```{r simulate}
library(powermean)
set.seed(417)

trade <- expand.grid(exporter = seq_len(12L), importer = seq_len(12L),
                     year = seq_len(8L))
trade <- trade[trade$exporter != trade$importer, ]
trade$pair <- interaction(trade$exporter, trade$importer, drop = TRUE)
adoption <- sample(2:12, nlevels(trade$pair), replace = TRUE)
trade$agreement <- as.integer(trade$year >= adoption[as.integer(trade$pair)])

log_mean <- 1.5 + 0.4 * trade$agreement +
    sin(trade$exporter * trade$year) / 5 + cos(trade$importer * trade$year) / 5
trade$value <- rpois(nrow(trade), exp(log_mean))
trade$value[as.integer(trade$pair) <= 2L] <- 0
```

## Fit PPML and check the sample

`ppml()` targets the arithmetic mean with Poisson working variance.
The caret combines identifiers within a fixed-effect block. The pair is
a separate block and supplies the covariance clusters.

```{r joint}
formula <- value ~ 0 + agreement | pair + exporter^year + importer^year
joint <- ppml(formula, trade, cluster = ~pair)
tidy(joint)

c(input = joint$sample$input_n, retained = joint$sample$nobs)
table(joint$sample$reason, useNA = "ifany")
```

The all-zero pairs are separated from the finite PPML fit. An individual
zero can remain in estimation when its pair trades in other years.
`joint$sample$positions` gives the one-based input row numbers to use
when aligning fitted means with the trade data.

## Cancel the pair effects

Cancelling pair effects eliminates the pair scale from the slope
equation. With `tau = 1`, the cancelled and joint PPML slopes agree on
the same retained sample. With `tau = 2`, cancellation uses Gamma working
variance and the slope equation changes. Both calls still target the
arithmetic mean.

```{r cancellation}
cancelled_ppml <- fit(formula, trade, cancel = "pair", tau = 1)
cancelled_gamma <- fit(formula, trade, cancel = "pair", tau = 2)

c(joint = unname(coef(joint)), cancelled = unname(coef(cancelled_ppml)))
etable(joint, cancelled_gamma, names = c("Joint PPML", "Cancelled Gamma"))
head(fixef(cancelled_gamma)$pair)
head(cbind(fitted = predict(cancelled_gamma), residual = residuals(cancelled_gamma)))
```

For the cancelled fit, `fixef()` includes recovered pair effects.
`predict()` recovers fitted means on the retained rows.
`residuals()` subtracts those means from the retained observations
here because the mean order is one. For replacement covariates,
preserve the retained row labels and order and keep the pair and
country-year identifiers fixed.

## Compare the bias adjustments

Request the short-group BBP coefficient correction on the cancelled fit.
For eligible three-way PPML panels, request the Weidner--Zylkin (WZ)
coefficient and pair covariance adjustments on the joint fit. The
correction columns from `tidy()` show the uncorrected point and the
estimated bias alongside the reported coefficient.

```{r adjustments}
bbp <- fit(formula, trade, cancel = "pair", tau = 2, bias_correction = TRUE)
wz <- ppml(formula, trade, bias_correction = "wz",
           vcov = list(cluster = "pair", adjustment = "wz"))

tidy(bbp)
tidy(wz)
```

BBP predictions use the corrected reporting point. The BBP covariance
uses the uncorrected point. WZ predictions use the original estimating
root, and the requested covariance applies its separate pair adjustment.
